test_title: PYST 41: RRB Group D - GS (Held On: 15 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: When thrown in soil, which of the following substances will persist in the environment for a long time?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Broken glass pieces**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Broken glass pieces** are categorized as **non-biodegradable** waste. This means they cannot be broken down or decomposed by the action of **microorganisms** like bacteria, fungi, or earthworms. ***Hence, option 2 is correct.***
 
• **Mango seeds** are organic matter derived from living organisms. They are **biodegradable** and will eventually rot and decompose into the soil, though they take slightly longer than soft tissues due to their hard shell. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Pieces of bread** consist of organic compounds like **carbohydrates**. They are highly **biodegradable** and are quickly decomposed by **molds** and bacteria when exposed to moisture in the soil. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Apple peels** are typical kitchen waste and are **biodegradable**. They decompose rapidly (usually within **few weeks**) and turn into **compost**, adding nutrients back to the environment. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• **Persistence in the environment** refers to the duration a substance remains in the soil without changing its chemical structure. **Glass** is made primarily of **silica (Silicon Dioxide)**, which is extremely stable and can persist for **1 million years** or more.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Biodegradable Substances:**

 
 
• These are substances that are degraded by **natural processes** into simpler, non-toxic substances.
 
• Examples include **agricultural residues**, **paper**, **wood**, **cloth**, and **animal dung**.
 
• The decomposition process is carried out by **decomposers**, which recycle nutrients back into the **ecosystem**.
 
 
 
• **Non-biodegradable Substances:**
 
 
• These substances do not degrade or take a **very long time** (hundreds to thousands of years) to break down.
 
• Common examples include **plastics**, **polythene bags**, **synthetic fibers**, **metal cans**, and **radioactive waste**.
 
• They often act as **pollutants** and can enter the **food chain**, leading to **biological magnification**.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact of Glass:**
 
 
• While **glass** is chemically **inert** and does not leach toxic chemicals like some plastics, its physical presence causes **land pollution**.
 
• In soil, **broken glass** poses a physical hazard to **macro-fauna** such as earthworms and can hinder the **penetration of plant roots**.
 
• Because it does not **oxidize** or **corrode** easily, it remains unchanged in the **geological strata** for eras.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Microbial Enzymes:** Microorganisms produce specific **enzymes** to break down organic bonds (like C-C or C-H bonds in food). However, they do not possess enzymes to break the **silicon-oxygen** bonds found in **glass**.
 
• **Waste Management:** To prevent environmental accumulation, **non-biodegradable** items like **glass** and **metals** should be **recycled**. Glass is **100% recyclable** and can be melted and reformed infinitely without loss in quality.
 
• **Decomposition Timeframes:** While an **apple peel** takes about **2 to 4 weeks** to disappear, a **plastic bottle** may take **450 years**, and **glass** effectively never disappears under normal environmental conditions.
